L230: 
L231: To be invited to apply for Victorian skilled visa nomination, you must first submit a Registration of Interest (ROI).
L232: The information you provide in your 【145†SkillSelect†immi.homeaffairs.gov.au】 Expression of Interest (EOI) with the Australian Government's Department of Home Affairs, and your ROI helps us to select applicants for Victorian visa nomination. An ROI is not an application for Victorian visa nomination.
L233: 
L234: When assessing your ROI we consider the information provided in your SkillSelect EOI. It is important to ensure that your EOI is always accurate and up to date.

L245: ### How do I submit a Registration of Interest (ROI) for Victorian visa nomination?
L246: 
L247: To submit an ROI for Victorian skilled visa nomination:
L248: 
L249:   1. Check your eligibility
L250: 
L251: Make sure you meet the requirements for the visa you are seeking nomination for - Skilled Nominated visa (subclass 190) or Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491).
L252: 
L253:   2. Submit your EOI
L254: 
L255: Submit or update your Expression of Interest (EOI) via the Australian Government’s SkillSelect.
L256:   3. Submit your ROI
L257: Using the EOI number received from SkillSelect, create an account on the 【5†Live in Melbourne portal†visa-nominations.liveinmelbourne.vic.gov.au】 and submit an ROI for Victorian skilled visa nomination.
L258: ### Previously submitted an ROI?
L259: 
L260: If you previously submitted an ROI in the 2024-25 and wish to be considered for invitation in the 2025-26 program, your ROI is still valid. You do not need to withdraw your ROI unless the information in the ROI has changed.
L261: 
L262: Your ROI will remain in our system for selection until it is withdrawn or selected.
L263: You can check if your ROI is active via the 【5†Live in Melbourne portal†visa-nominations.liveinmelbourne.vic.gov.au】. Login to your account > Applications > Click into the relevant NFR number > If active, the status will show  'Submitted' or ‘Received’.
L264: ### Invitation rounds
L265: 
L266: Invitation rounds occur throughout the year. There are no set dates for invitation rounds. The program will close to new ROIs in 2026, at a date to be advised.
L267: 
L268: An 【72†ROI】 is not an application for Victorian visa nomination, and as such is not subject to a processing timeframe.
L269: 
L270: If you have submitted an ROI but have not received an email inviting you to apply for Victorian nomination, you cannot apply for nomination.
L271: 
L272: There is no guarantee that your ROI will be selected.
L273: If your ROI is assessed as eligible but not yet selected, it will remain under consideration for the selection rounds later in the year.
L274: ### ROI ranking factors
L275: 
L276: All ROIs are ranked against each other and the most competitive across a combination of ranking factors are invited. Nomination places are limited, and as such this process is highly competitive and invitation is not guaranteed.
L277: 
L278: When inviting ROIs, we consider the following ranking factors according to the information you have provided in your EOI and ROI:
L279:   * age,
L280:   * English language level,
L281:   * years of experience in your nominated occupation,
L282:   * education level,
L283:   * occupation skill level,
L284:   * partner’s skill (if applicable), and
L285:   * salary – onshore candidates only.
L286: 
L287: If your partner is an Australian citizen or permanent resident, you cannot claim partner points in your ROI.
L288: 
L289: Certain occupations in the following industry sectors will also be prioritised:
L290:   * Health
L291:   * Social services
L292:   * Education (including early childhood)
L293:   * Construction
L294:   * New Energy
L295:   * Advanced manufacturing
L296:   * Hospitality and tourism – for the 491 visa
L297: 
L298: For subclass 491 applicants living overseas, the following industry sectors will be prioritised:
L299: 
L300:   * Health
L301:   * Social Services
L302:   * Education (including Early Childhood)
L303: ### Annual earnings estimation
L304: 
L305: If you indicate in your ROI that you are currently living and working in skilled employment in Victoria or regional Victoria, you will be asked to provide an estimate of your annual earnings.
L306: 
L307: Skilled employment includes any role that is at skill levels 1, 2 or 3 in the relevant 【147†ANZSCO classification†www.abs.gov.au】.
L308: Your earnings are one of many factors used to select ROIs for invitation. There is no minimum experience or hours of work required to be eligible for Victorian visa nomination. Please see 【76†Annual earnings estimation guide】 for information on how to calculate this figure.
L309: ### Further information about ROI
L310: 
L311: Once you have submitted an ROI, it will remain in our system until either withdrawn by you, invited by us or the program year ends. You cannot update an ROI once it has been submitted.
L312: 
L313: What if the information provided in my ROI has changed?
L314: 
L315: The information in your ROI must be accurate and up to date. If you are invited to apply for visa nomination but unable to provide evidence for your claims, your application may be refused.
L316: If the information in your ROI is incorrect or out of date, you must withdraw it and submit a new ROI. You cannot update and re‑submit a previous ROI.
L317: 
L318: You only need to withdraw and submit a new ROI, if the information entered has changed, including:
L319: 
L320:   * Annual earnings,
L321:   * Visa subclass,
L322:   * Partner points claimed in your ROI
L323:   * SkillSelect EOI number
L324: Withdrawing and submitting a new ROI will not affect the ranking or position of your ROI in our assessment and does not negatively impact your chances of selection.
L325: 
L326: How do I withdraw my existing ROI?
L327: 
L328: Login to your account > Applications tab > NFR number > click withdraw.
L329: 
L330: You can withdraw your ROI via the 【5†Live in Melbourne portal†visa-nominations.liveinmelbourne.vic.gov.au】.
L331: 
L332: Do I need to attach documents to my ROI?
L333: We do not require any documents to be provided in the ROI. If you are selected, attach relevant documents in your nomination application.
L334: 
L335: See 【74†Skilled Nominated visa (subclass 190)】 or 【75†Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491)】 for further information about eligibility and documents required.
L336: 
L337: How do I know if my ROI is active?
L338: You can check if your ROI is active through the 【5†Live in Melbourne portal†visa-nominations.liveinmelbourne.vic.gov.au】. Login to your account > Applications > Click into the relevant NFR number > If active, the status will show 'Submitted' or ‘Received’.
L339: 
L340: 【148†Image: A screenshot of the of an ROI showing the active status】
L341: 
L342: Can I have more than one ROI?
L343: 
L344: You can only have one active ROI submitted at any time.
L345: You cannot submit a separate ROI for each subclass or nominated occupation. If you wish to change the subclass, or anything else on your ROI, you must withdraw the existing ROI and submit a new ROI.
L346: 
L347: How long is the invitation to apply for Victorian visa nomination valid for?
L348: 
L349: If you are invited to apply you, or your agent (if applicable), will be notified via email. You will need to submit your nomination application before the invitation expires.
L350: We will not reissue the invitation if you do not apply within the specified period. If you wish to be considered in future invitation rounds, you will need to submit a new ROI.
L351: 
L352: What is the fee to submit an ROI?
L353: 
L354: Victorian ROI and nomination are free of charge. When you submit your visa application with the Department of Home Affairs, you will need to pay the visa fee.
L355: ### Updating and withdrawing your existing EOI
L356: 
L357: What if the information in my SkillSelect EOI has changed?
L358: 
L359: If the information in your SkillSelect EOI or the EOI points have changed, you do not need to withdraw and submit a new ROI. You only need to withdraw and submit a new ROI if the information you entered on the ROI form changes.
L360: However, it is important that your EOI is accurate and up to date. If you are invited to apply for visa nomination but unable to evidence your claims, your application may be refused. This includes years of experience in your nominated occupation and where you are currently living.
L361: 
L362: Please review your EOI in SkillSelect and ensure the information is up to date and is consistent with the ROI information you have provided in your Live in Melbourne account.
L363: If you are invited to apply, you cannot modify your EOI. Please 【149†Contact Us】 about the information you wish to update on your EOI if you have been invited to apply.
L364: 
L365: What if I have a new SkillSelect EOI number?
L366: 
L367: Please withdraw your existing ROI and submit a new one. You must create a new EOI if your existing one is expiring within the next 12 months.

L244: ## General skilled visa nomination questions
L245: 
L246: ##
L247: ### Where in Victoria does a nominated visa allow me to live?
L248: 
L249: The 【74†Skilled Nominated visa (subclass 190)】 is a permanent visa allowing you to live and work anywhere in the state of Victoria, including Melbourne.
L250: 
L251: The 【75†Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491)】 is a provisional (5 year) visa with a pathway to permanent residence after living and working in regional Victoria for at least 3 years.
L252: ### What are the conditions of Victorian visa nomination?
L253: 
L254: The conditions of Victorian visa nomination are outlined on the 【74†Skilled Nominated subclass 190】 and 【75†Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) subclass 491 visa】 pages.
L255: 
L256: ### How many points do I need to be selected to apply for Victorian visa nomination?
L257: 
L258: You must have at least 65 points (including points awarded for state nomination) to be nominated by Victoria.
